test: none: open on SolidCraft main (solidcore); the geometry is the report's script (box, cylinder along a tilted axis, join, fillet)
summary: A 1 mm round at the foot of a cylinder boss whose axis leans a few degrees off square to the block it is joined to is refused on SolidCraft main (#14000) with 'SMLib fillet: operation: SMLib failed (status 1001)' since 59a85a164 (#13900, tangency-labs/solidcore#3066, 'a circle-class round is certified on its own torus'); its parent 4890cebd3 builds it. The geometry is the report's script: a block 40 x 40 x 10 at (-20, -20, 0), a boss of radius 5 and height 15 from (0, 0, 5) along (sin a, 0, cos a) (sunk 5 into the block), joined, and a 1 mm round on the boss's foot, picked at (5 tan a, 5, 10). Replayed with solidcraft-cli built from main ef966d46 and from 4890cebd3 (2026-11-09; main 8babea5c gave the same at 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5): on main the round is refused at 0.25, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5 and 4 degrees and builds at 0, 3 and 5; on 4890cebd3 it builds at every tilt (the report saw 0.5 to 2 refused on Linux, to 3 on macOS: the band moves with rounding). The report traces it to keep_definition in blend/fillet_exact.rs, which runs with fillet_round_as_definition: the commit replaced keep_round_if_proved, which kept a round without its definition when its certificate failed within the body's tolerance, with round.recertify(k, surface)?, so a canal-class round (its spine is an ellipse when the boss leans) whose spine, computed in floating point, is not exactly on the faces' offsets now refuses the fillet ('the spine is off the faces' offsets'). The cases run with the two fixes that reach it, both on in SolidCraft's fixes(): fillet_exact_round_classes (the round built by its class) and fillet_round_as_definition (the round keeps its definition). With both, every tilt gives the verdict it gives with all of SolidCraft's fixes; with either alone, or with all of SolidCraft's fixes but fillet_round_as_definition, every tilt builds. No fix yet. The cases are box, cylinder, union and fillet steps at tilts 0 (the control, a torus round), 0.25, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3 and 5 degrees. Volume: the block 16000, the boss above the block's top 25 pi (15 - 5 / cos a) (a cylinder cut on a slant holds pi r^2 times its axis length), and the round, a pipe of radius 1 about the ellipse where z = 11 meets the boss offset by 1, integrated in tube coordinates about that ellipse (Gauss-Legendre across the section, split at the foot, and the trapezoid rule along the spine; converged to 1e-13 mm^3). At 0 the round is a torus section and the total has the closed form 16000 + 250 pi + (1 - pi/4) 2 pi (5 + (10 - 3 pi)/(12 - 3 pi)). Checked by a randomised QMC of the round (scrambled Sobol, 64 replicates of 2^22 points, within one standard error at every tilt), and against 4890cebd3's volumes (within 1e-6 mm^3 at every tilt). The tolerance, 0.001 mm^3, is above the volume integral's 1e-8 relative accuracy (1.7e-4 mm^3 here) plus what a round anywhere within the bodies' 1e-5 mm tolerance of the exact one could change (1e-5 times its 53 mm^2, 5.3e-4 mm^3), and below what a round that ignores the tilt changes from 1 degree up (0.003 mm^3 at 1 degree) or a radius 0.1% off (0.014 mm^3). The result is one lump and a manifold solid. Expected values are analytic; nothing comes from a commercial CAD product.
